correctness.rationale: Gale evenness is reduced to k-matchings in the n-cycle. Each proper induced subgraph is a union of paths, so alpha(Y)=|Y|-nu(Y). The maximum complement is h+k-1 and equality implies a maximum cycle-independent set plus exactly k-1 vertices. The cyclic binary run proof divides all odd-n optimizers into two exhaustive, uniquely rooted classes. The independent verifier tested 34 parameter configurations and 1232 direct Gale facets; finite tests corroborate the analytic proof.

evidence: The 2021 Proposition 3.6 formula is tau=ceil((n-2k)/2)+1, identical to our admitted tau value, so that part is covered.
The new minimum-solution number is 2*C(h,k-1) for even n and n*C(h,k-1) for odd n. These distinct counts cannot be deduced from the tau value alone; the proof classifies all maximum facet-free sets.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The old theorem implies only the minimum size, not uniqueness or number of minimizers. The new result is the stronger complete equality-case classification, with a nontrivial parity difference in its enumeration; it does not rebrand the known tau identity.

value.rationale: The number and full structure of optimal facet transversals are natural extremizer data for the transversal-ratio invariant. The formula applies uniformly to all even dimensions, with a sharp parity bifurcation in polynomial growth: n^(k-1) versus n^k at fixed dimension 2k. This is not determined by the known minimum cardinality and helps distinguish stability and abundance of optimizers.
